questions.stem: In organic chemistry, what is a functional group?
options: A family of compounds sharing a general formula and differing by CH₂
The part of a molecule that contains only carbon and hydrogen atoms
An atom or group of atoms that gives a compound its characteristic reactions
The longest continuous chain of carbon atoms, which gives the compound its name
questions.explanation: A functional group, such as -OH or -COOH, is the reactive part of a molecule and decides how the compound behaves. The longest carbon chain is the parent chain, and a family differing by CH₂ is a homologous series.

questions.stem: What is the systematic name of the ester CH₃COOCH₂CH₃?
questions.explanation: The CH₃CO- part comes from ethanoic acid and the -OCH₂CH₃ part from ethanol, so the ester is ethyl ethanoate: the alcohol part is named first, then the acid part with -oate. Methyl propanoate, CH₃CH₂COOCH₃, is an isomer with the carbons arranged differently.

questions.stem: How is CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ named and classified?
questions.explanation: The -OH is on carbon 2 of a three-carbon chain, so it is propan-2-ol. The carbon carrying the -OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms, which makes it a secondary alcohol; a tertiary alcohol needs three.

questions.stem: Which of these alcohols is a tertiary alcohol?
questions.explanation: In 2-methylpropan-2-ol, (CH₃)₃COH, the carbon bearing the -OH is bonded to three other carbons. Butan-2-ol is secondary, and 2-methylpropan-1-ol and butan-1-ol are primary, because their -OH carbon has only one carbon neighbour.

questions.stem: Which name matches the compound CH₃CONH₂?
questions.explanation: The -CONH₂ group, a carbonyl joined to nitrogen, is an amide, and with two carbons in total the compound is ethanamide. Ethanamine (also called aminoethane) is CH₃CH₂NH₂, which has an -NH₂ group but no carbonyl.

questions.stem: Amino acids, the building units of proteins, contain which two functional groups?
options: An amine group and a carboxylic acid group
A hydroxyl group and a carboxylic acid group
An amide group and an ester group
An amine group and a hydroxyl group
questions.explanation: An amino acid has an amine (-NH₂) group and a carboxylic acid (-COOH) group attached to a hydrocarbon chain. Amide groups appear only once amino acids have joined together into peptides.

questions.stem: Chloroethane has a higher boiling point than ethane. Which explanation is correct?
options: The covalent bonds within chloroethane molecules are stronger than those in ethane
Chloroethane is an ionic compound, so its particles are held in a lattice
Its polar C-Cl bond adds dipole-dipole forces, and its extra electrons strengthen dispersion forces
Chloroethane molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other through the chlorine atom
questions.explanation: Replacing an H with Cl makes the molecule polar and gives it many more electrons, so both dipole-dipole and dispersion forces between molecules increase. Hydrogen bonding needs H bonded to N, O or F, which chloroethane does not have, and boiling never breaks covalent bonds within molecules.

questions.stem: 1-chloropropane is warmed with aqueous sodium hydroxide. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: The hydroxide ion substitutes for the chlorine on the same carbon, giving propan-1-ol and sodium chloride. The -OH replaces the halogen where it was, so propan-2-ol would need 2-chloropropane. Making propanal or propanoic acid needs an oxidising agent.

questions.stem: Why do alkyl halides undergo substitution reactions more readily than the alkanes they were made from?
options: Alkyl halides contain carbon-carbon double bonds that open up easily
The halogen atom makes the molecule ionic, so it dissociates in water
Alkyl halides are gases at room temperature, so their molecules collide more
The polar carbon-halogen bond leaves the carbon open to attack by negative ions
questions.explanation: The halogen pulls electron density away from the carbon, giving it a partial positive charge that attracts ions such as OH⁻, which then replace the halogen. Alkyl halides are covalent and saturated; they have no double bonds and do not dissociate into ions.

questions.stem: A chemist wants to make the tertiary alcohol 2-methylpropan-2-ol by a substitution reaction with hydroxide ions. Which alkyl halide should be used?
questions.explanation: Substitution puts the -OH where the halogen was. In 2-chloro-2-methylpropane the chlorine is on a carbon bonded to three other carbons, so the product is the tertiary alcohol. 1-chloro-2-methylpropane would give a primary alcohol, and 2-chlorobutane the secondary butan-2-ol.

questions.stem: Which description of the structure of benzene, C₆H₆, is correct?
options: An open chain of six carbon atoms containing three double bonds
A flat ring in which all six carbon-carbon bonds are the same length
A flat ring of alternating short double bonds and long single bonds
A puckered ring of six single bonds, like cyclohexane
questions.explanation: Benzene is a flat, symmetrical hexagon in which every carbon-carbon bond is intermediate between a single and a double bond, so all six are the same length. This is why it is drawn as a hexagon with a circle inside, and why it is very stable.

questions.stem: Ethanol and propane have similar molar masses, but ethanol boils at 78 °C and propane at −42 °C. Why?
options: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
Ethanol has stronger covalent bonds within its molecules
Ethanol has far more electrons, so its dispersion forces are stronger
Ethanol molecules are held together by ionic bonds
questions.explanation: The O-H group lets ethanol molecules hydrogen bond to one another, which takes much more energy to overcome than the dispersion forces between propane molecules. The two molecules have the same number of electrons (26), so dispersion forces are similar.

questions.stem: Why does ethanol mix completely with water while ethane is almost insoluble?
options: Ethane molecules are too large to fit between water molecules
Ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water molecules
Ethanol ionises in water to release hydroxide ions
Ethanol reacts with water to form ethanoic acid
questions.explanation: The -OH group of ethanol hydrogen bonds with water, so ethanol molecules fit into water's hydrogen-bonded network. Ethane is non-polar and cannot do this. Ethanol does not ionise or react with water to any real extent.

questions.stem: Ethane-1,2-diol, HOCH₂CH₂OH, boils at a much higher temperature than ethanol. What is the main reason?
options: It forms covalent bonds between neighbouring molecules when liquid
Each molecule has two -OH groups, so it forms more hydrogen bonds
Its molecules are ionic, so a lattice must be broken to boil it
Its carbon-oxygen bonds are double bonds, which are harder to break
questions.explanation: A polyalcohol has more -OH groups per molecule, so each molecule can take part in more hydrogen bonds and more energy is needed to separate them. Like ethanol, it is a covalent molecular substance with single C-O bonds.

questions.stem: A small piece of sodium is added to ethanol. What are the products?
questions.explanation: Sodium replaces the hydrogen of the -OH group: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂O⁻Na⁺ + H₂. The bubbles are hydrogen. Sodium ethanoate forms from ethanoic acid, not ethanol.

questions.stem: Propan-1-ol is warmed with a limited amount of acidified dichromate solution, and the product is distilled off as it forms. What is the main product?
questions.explanation: Mild or limited oxidation turns a primary alcohol into an aldehyde, and distilling it off stops further oxidation. With excess oxidant the aldehyde would go on to propanoic acid. Propanone is a ketone, formed from the secondary alcohol propan-2-ol.

questions.stem: Propan-1-ol is heated with excess acidified permanganate solution. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: A strong oxidant in excess oxidises a primary alcohol all the way through the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid. Propanal is only the main product when the oxidation is limited and the aldehyde is removed.

questions.stem: Butan-2-ol is oxidised with acidified permanganate solution. What is the organic product?
questions.explanation: Oxidising a secondary alcohol gives a ketone, so butan-2-ol forms butanone. Aldehydes and carboxylic acids come from primary alcohols, and but-2-ene would come from removing water, which is not an oxidation.

questions.stem: Butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol are each warmed with acidified dichromate. Which one leaves the solution orange?
options: None of them, as all are oxidised
questions.explanation: Dichromate turns from orange to green when it oxidises an alcohol. Primary butan-1-ol and secondary butan-2-ol are both oxidised, but 2-methylpropan-2-ol is tertiary, so it is not oxidised and the solution stays orange.

questions.stem: Why are tertiary alcohols not oxidised by acidified dichromate or permanganate?
options: Tertiary alcohols do not dissolve in acidified solutions
The -OH group of a tertiary alcohol is bonded to two carbon atoms
Tertiary alcohols cannot take part in hydrogen bonding
The carbon bonded to the -OH has no hydrogen atom attached to it
questions.explanation: Oxidising an alcohol removes a hydrogen from the carbon that carries the -OH. In a tertiary alcohol that carbon is bonded to three carbons and the -OH, so it has no hydrogen to lose. An -OH group bonds to just one carbon, whatever the class of alcohol.

questions.stem: Why can an aldehyde be oxidised to a carboxylic acid when a ketone cannot be oxidised further?
options: An aldehyde is a stronger acid, so it reacts with oxidants more easily
A ketone has a triple bond that protects it from oxidation
An aldehyde has a hydrogen on its carbonyl carbon, but a ketone does not
A ketone has no oxygen atom, so oxidants cannot react with it
questions.explanation: In an aldehyde the C=O carbon carries a hydrogen, which can be replaced by -OH to give -COOH. In a ketone the C=O carbon is bonded to two carbons, so oxidation would mean breaking a carbon-carbon bond. Ketones do contain oxygen, in the C=O group.

questions.stem: Propanal is less soluble in water than propan-1-ol, the alcohol it is made from. Why?
options: Propanal is a non-polar molecule, so water molecules cannot attract it
Propanal has a larger molar mass, so its dispersion forces resist dissolving
Propanal reacts with water to form an insoluble carboxylic acid
Propanal has no O-H group, so it forms fewer hydrogen bonds with water
questions.explanation: Propan-1-ol can both donate and accept hydrogen bonds through its O-H group, but propanal's C=O oxygen can only accept them, so it interacts less with water. Propanal is polar, and its molar mass (58) is slightly less than propan-1-ol's (60).

questions.stem: Ethene decolourises bromine water rapidly in the dark, but ethane reacts with bromine only in UV light. How are these two reactions classified?
options: Both undergo substitution, but ethene reacts faster
Ethene undergoes addition and ethane undergoes substitution
Ethene undergoes substitution and ethane undergoes addition
Both undergo addition, but ethane needs UV light to start
questions.explanation: The C=C double bond in ethene opens and bromine adds across it, giving 1,2-dibromoethane. Ethane is saturated, so in UV light a bromine atom replaces a hydrogen atom, giving bromoethane and HBr: a substitution.

questions.stem: Propene reacts with hydrogen bromide. Which pair of products can form?
questions.explanation: HBr is an asymmetric molecule, so its H and Br can add across the double bond either way round. The Br can end up on carbon 1 or carbon 2, giving two isomers. 1,2-dibromopropane would need Br₂, not HBr.

questions.stem: But-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, is reacted with steam over an acid catalyst. What forms?
options: A mixture of butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol
questions.explanation: Water adds across the double bond. But-2-ene is symmetrical, so whichever carbon gains the -OH the product is butan-2-ol. A mixture of isomers forms only when the alkene is asymmetric, as with but-1-ene.

questions.stem: Ethyne reacts completely with excess hydrogen over a nickel catalyst. What is the product?
questions.explanation: The triple bond can add two molecules of hydrogen. With excess hydrogen and complete reaction, ethyne goes through ethene to the saturated ethane. Ethene would only be the product if the reaction stopped after one addition.

questions.stem: Which balanced equation shows propane burning in a limited supply of oxygen to form carbon monoxide and water only?
questions.explanation: Six CO and eight H₂O contain 6 + 8 = 14 oxygen atoms, which needs 7O₂ for two propane molecules. The 5O₂ version is not balanced, the CO₂ equation is complete combustion, and the equation giving carbon describes soot rather than carbon monoxide.

questions.stem: A plastics plant needs a monomer for addition polymerisation. Which of these compounds would be suitable?
questions.explanation: Addition polymerisation needs a C=C double bond that can open and link to neighbouring monomers. Chloroethene, CH₂=CHCl, has one and forms poly(chloroethene), PVC. The other molecules are saturated.

questions.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, undergoes addition polymerisation. Which structure shows one repeating unit of the polymer formed?
questions.explanation: When propene polymerises, its double bond opens and only the two carbons of the double bond join the chain, so the -CH₃ hangs off every second carbon. The polymer is saturated, so a repeating unit containing a double bond cannot be right.

questions.stem: Which pair of monomers could react to form a polyester?
questions.explanation: A polyester needs a polyalcohol and a polyacid, so that each monomer can form an ester link at both ends and the chain keeps growing, with water released at each link. Ethanol has only one -OH group, so it caps the chain instead of extending it, and two diols cannot form ester links with each other.

questions.stem: Why is the pH of 0.1 mol L⁻¹ ethanoic acid higher than that of 0.1 mol L⁻¹ hydrochloric acid?
options: Ethanoic acid has fewer hydrogen atoms in each molecule
Ethanoic acid ionises only partly, so its hydrogen ion concentration is lower
Ethanoic acid is more dilute than hydrochloric acid at the same concentration
Ethanoic acid releases hydroxide ions as well as hydrogen ions
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids are weak acids: only a small fraction of the molecules donate a proton, while HCl ionises completely. Fewer H⁺ ions means a higher pH. The two solutions are equally concentrated, and CH₃COOH actually has four hydrogens, of which only one is acidic.

questions.stem: Ethanedioic acid, HOOC-COOH, is classified as which kind of acid?
options: A polyalcohol, because it contains two -OH groups
A polyacid, because each molecule can donate two protons
A monoacid, because only one of its hydrogen atoms is acidic
A strong acid, because it has two carboxyl groups
questions.explanation: Each of its two -COOH groups can donate a proton, so it is a diacid, a type of polyacid. Having two carboxyl groups does not make it strong; it still ionises only partly. Its -OH groups are part of carboxyl groups, so it is not an alcohol.

questions.stem: What are the products when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium hydrogen carbonate?
options: Sodium hydroxide, ethanol and carbon dioxide
Sodium ethanoate, water and carbon dioxide
Sodium ethanoate and hydrogen gas only
Ethyl ethanoate, water and sodium oxide
questions.explanation: Like other acids, a carboxylic acid reacts with a hydrogen carbonate to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂. Hydrogen gas forms when an acid reacts with a reactive metal.

questions.stem: Which balanced equation shows ethanoic acid reacting with magnesium?
questions.explanation: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺, so two ethanoate ions (CH₃COO⁻) are needed in the salt, and the acid's hydrogen is released as H₂ gas. A single ethanoate with Mg leaves the charges unbalanced, and water forms with oxides or hydroxides, not metals.

questions.stem: Propanoic acid is heated with methanol and a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid. Which ester forms?
questions.explanation: The ester is named with the alcohol part first (methyl, from methanol) and the acid part second (propanoate, from propanoic acid). Propyl methanoate would come from propan-1-ol and methanoic acid. Sulfuric acid is the catalyst.

questions.stem: Which properties are typical of small esters such as ethyl ethanoate?
options: Distinctive smells and low solubility in water
High boiling points from strong hydrogen bonding
Acidic solutions that turn blue litmus red
Rapid oxidation to ketones in air
questions.explanation: Esters have no O-H group, so they cannot hydrogen bond to each other and have fairly low boiling points; they are only slightly soluble in water. Many have fruity or distinctive smells and are used in flavours and perfumes. They are not acids.

questions.stem: Ethyl ethanoate is heated under reflux with sodium hydroxide solution. What are the products?
questions.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis breaks the ester link. The acid part ends up as its salt, sodium ethanoate, because the excess hydroxide neutralises the acid, and the alcohol part is released as ethanol.

questions.stem: Why does ethanamine, CH₃CH₂NH₂, have a much higher boiling point than propane, which has a similar molar mass?
options: The C-N bond is much stronger than any bond in propane
Ethanamine has a carbonyl group that attracts other molecules
The N-H bonds allow hydrogen bonding between ethanamine molecules
Ethanamine is ionic, with NH₂⁻ ions in a crystal lattice
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonded to nitrogen can form hydrogen bonds to the lone pair on another molecule's nitrogen, so more energy is needed to separate amine molecules than the dispersion-bonded propane molecules. Boiling separates molecules; it does not break bonds such as C-N.

questions.stem: Using ethene as the only source of carbon, which sequence of reactions could make ethyl ethanoate?
options: Add steam to make ethanol, oxidise part of it to ethanoic acid, then esterify the acid with the rest
Add HCl to make chloroethane, oxidise it to ethanoic acid, then add steam to form the ester
Oxidise ethene directly to ethanoic acid, then add steam to the acid to form the ester
Polymerise ethene, hydrolyse the polymer to ethanol, then oxidise the ethanol to the ester
questions.explanation: Ethyl ethanoate needs both ethanol and ethanoic acid. Steam adds to ethene to give ethanol; oxidising some of it with excess acidified permanganate gives ethanoic acid; heating the two with an acid catalyst forms the ester. Steam does not convert an acid into an ester.

questions.stem: Biodiesel is made by reacting plant oils with methanol to form methyl esters. Which type of reaction is used?
questions.explanation: Biodiesel molecules are methyl esters, made by transesterification: methanol swaps places with glycerol in the triglycerides of the oil. Addition polymerisation needs C=C monomers and makes long polymer chains, not fuel-sized molecules.
